A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 25-page paper, including supplementary material. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching text, equations, tables, and figures, apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v4 reports original caption analyses, model-output and fine-tuning experiments in Sections 2–4, and translation-evaluation and image-captioning human studies in Sections 8.1 and 8.3.

after.justification: v5 retains the same original caption analyses, model experiments, and human-study results, including their supplementary tables and examples.

M1.justification: The translation, scene-graph construction and union, expressive-coverage measurement, and fine-tuning procedures in Sections 2–4 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Crossmodal and Visual Genome coverage, seven-language selection, five-language LLaVA subset, and English/Japanese captioning study. No dataset, task, population, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical throughout, including the multimodel comparisons in Section 3.2 and Tables 12–13. No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation settings are identical, including translation preprocessing, caption-set construction, the 1.8k-image training and holdout sets, SPICE evaluation, and human-study sample sizes.

E4.justification: Both retain the same language-mode comparison, Visual Genome grounding analysis, translation-artifact checks, untranslated multilingual-embedding experiment, cumulative scene-graph analysis, and qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including p < 0.001 in Table 5 and Bonferroni-corrected comparisons in Table 13. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match. This includes the fine-tuning matrices in Tables 4, 14, and 15 and the supplementary semantic and expressive results.

T1.justification: The scene-graph and expressive-coverage definitions, formal comparison expressions, and intersection reasoning in Sections 2–4 and 9.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about cross-language semantic and expressive variation, language-specific fine-tuning behavior, and the potential value of multilingual training.

C2.justification: Interpretations of language modes, translation effects, and multilingual training are identical. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning language coverage, experimental scale, and linguistic essentialism.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, translation and multilingual-generation prompts, human-study instructions, and other experimental details are unchanged. No implementation or resource-access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 6, the in-text citations, and all 129 reference entries are identical, preserving the same research positioning.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v4 dated 29 Mar 2025 to v5 dated 12 May 2025. All other wording, headings, and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and page layouts are unchanged, including the supplementary material. Rendered differences are confined to the version/date text recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: The only visible or textual revision is the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, reproducibility information, and visual presentation otherwise match throughout both PDFs, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
